body.statement: On the fixed known support \(H\) defining \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\), is the uniform excess-endpoint rate \(\{\log n/n\}^{\beta/(2\beta+2)}+n^{-1/2}\) minimax, up to logarithmic factors, along sequences of laws \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\) for which \(R(P)\to0\)? More sharply, can a matching lower bound distinguish the cost of estimating the obstacle boundary from the cost of estimating the signed objective? A shrinking support-hole transition lies outside \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\) and requires a separately defined varying-support triangular-array class.
body.justification: The upper rate becomes economically interpretable only after determining whether its obstacle and signed-objective terms are unavoidable along fixed-support sequences with \(R(P)\to0\).
body.gap: The known fixed rectangle support and uniform positive density lower bound exclude a shrinking support-hole transition from \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\). Existing results provide neither a matching fixed-support lower bound nor a separately formalized varying-support class.
body.consumer: A matching fixed-support lower bound would show whether shorter uniformly honest sensitivity intervals require stronger functional restrictions or merely a better estimator; a support-topology claim must await a distinct class.

obligation.what_is_open: A matching minimax lower bound, uniform along fixed-support sequences in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\) with \(R(P)\to0\), that separately attributes endpoint loss to estimating the obstacle boundary and to estimating the signed objective; any support-topology transition additionally requires a separately defined varying-support triangular-array class.
obligation.obstruction: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\), \(H=\bigcup_{R\in\mathscr R}R\) is the same known finite rectangle union and \(f_{XZ}\ge f_0>0\) throughout \(H\). Hence the suggested shrinking-hole family is outside the frozen class. Within fixed \(H\), the primitives establish the upper bound but supply no verified two-point or hypercube family that simultaneously remains in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\), has bounded product-experiment divergence, preserves nonempty obstacle feasibility, and separates an optimized WAOSS endpoint at the asserted rate.
obligation.attempted: The natural route perturbs \(g\) by a local \(\beta\)-H\"older bump and perturbs \(\nu_P\) to isolate the two error sources. A shrinking hole violates fixed support; on fixed support, verifying the density bounds, outcome bounds, obstacle compatibility, divergence bound, and optimized-endpoint separation is precisely the missing least-favorable-family construction. Assuming those properties would assume the crux.
obligation.partial_result: The established theorem gives the uniform upper endpoint error \(O(\{\log n/n\}^{\beta/(2\beta+2)}+n^{-1/2})\). Moreover, the support restriction itself yields a sharp scope conclusion: because \(H\) is the fixed known rectangle union and \(f_{XZ}\ge f_0>0\) on it, support topology cannot approach failure within \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\). Therefore the current minimax problem can vary \(R(P)\to0\) only on fixed \(H\); a shrinking-hole lower bound belongs to a new varying-support class. No matching fixed-support lower bound or decomposition into obstacle and signed-objective costs follows from the frozen primitives.
